title: Analytical Retrieval of Material Parameters in Monolayer Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides Based on a Solvable Exciton Model
authors: Duy-Nhat Ly, Thanh-Son Nguyen, Ngoc-Tram D. Hoang, Van-Hoang Le
abstract: We develop an analytical procedure to retrieve fundamental material parameters of monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides from optical and magneto-optical exciton spectra, based on the solvable modified Kratzer model. The proposed retrieval procedure naturally consists of two complementary stages. In the first stage, explicit inversion formulas determine the quasiparticle bandgap, effective screening parameter, and energy scaling factor directly from the experimentally measured energies of the three lowest excitonic states, from which the screening length is subsequently obtained. In the second stage, an analytical expression for the magnetic-field dependence of the exciton energies independently yields the reduced exciton mass, from which the surrounding dielectric constant is then calculated. Once the complete set of material parameters has been retrieved, the framework analytically predicts the diamagnetic coefficients, exciton radii, and complete magnetoexciton spectra without introducing additional fitting parameters or matrix diagonalization. The method is applied to a broad range of experimental samples for WSe$_2$, WS$_2$, MoS$_2$, MoSe$_2$, and MoTe$_2$ monolayers embedded in different dielectric environments. The retrieved material parameters are in good agreement with independent experimental measurements and previous Rytova--Keldysh (RK) calculations, while the predicted excitonic properties accurately reproduce available magneto-optical observations. The proposed analytical theory provides an efficient, physically transparent alternative to conventional numerical fitting procedures and offers an effective tool for the rapid characterization of two-dimensional semiconductors via excitonic spectroscopy.
summary: This paper introduces an advanced analytical framework to extract fundamental material properties from excitonic spectroscopy data of 2D semiconductor monolayers. By utilizing two complementary stages—analyzing zero-field spectra and then the magnetic field dependence—the authors derive parameters like bandgap, screening length, and exciton mass without needing additional fitting parameters. This offers a powerful, physically transparent tool for characterizing TMDs.
main_problem: The goal is to develop an analytical procedure to retrieve fundamental material parameters of monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) from their optical and magneto-optical exciton spectra.
main_result: The proposed two-stage analytical framework successfully determines key parameters like the bandgap, screening length, reduced exciton mass, and dielectric constant with high accuracy.
method: It employs an analytical inversion procedure based on solving equations derived from the solvable modified Kratzer model, avoiding iterative fitting or matrix diagonalization.
model_or_system: The study focuses on excitons in monolayer TMDCs (e.g., WSe2, MoS2) embedded in various dielectric environments. The physics is modeled using an exciton Hamiltonian solved via basis set expansion for magnetoexciton spectra.
key_observables: Exciton energies ($E_n$), the ratio of energy differences ($\Delta_{	ext{exp}}$), and the magnetic-field dependence of exciton energies $E_n(B)$.
important_parameters: Quasiparticle bandgap ($E_g$), effective screening parameter ($\xi$), energy scaling factor ($\eta$), reduced exciton mass ($\mu$), and surrounding dielectric constant ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the solvable modified Kratzer model approximation for describing excitonic binding energies, which is an analytical simplification of the full physics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between theoretical predictions (using the derived formulas) and experimental/numerical results for magnetoexciton spectra across different TMDCs and magnetic fields.
paper_structure: The paper details a two-stage retrieval process: Stage 1 uses zero-field exciton energies ($E_1, E_2, E_3$) to find $\xi$, $\eta$, and $E_g$; Stage 2 uses the field dependence of these energies to independently determine $\mu$ and subsequently $\kappa$.
why_interesting: The analytical nature of the retrieval method provides a highly transparent and efficient alternative to complex numerical fitting routines, which is valuable for rapid characterization in quantum optics.
